name: Aizoaceae
description: Pigfaces, ice plants and warrigal greens: fleshy-leaved plants that cope with salt and drought.

name: Amaranthaceae
description: Includes beetroot, silverbeet, spinach and many saltbushes.

name: Amaryllidaceae
description: Bulbs and strappy plants, including agapanthus, clivias and the onion family.

name: Anacardiaceae
description: The cashew family, including mangoes and the weedy broad-leaf pepper tree.

toxic.note: The sap of many members can irritate the skin.

name: Apiaceae
description: The carrot family: carrots, parsley, coriander, dill and fennel. Their flat flower heads feed hoverflies and tiny parasitic wasps.

name: Apocynaceae
description: The dogbane family, including frangipani and star jasmine. Many members have milky sap.

name: Araceae
description: The arum family, including monstera and philodendrons.

toxic.note: The leaves and stems contain calcium oxalate crystals that irritate the mouth and throat.

name: Arecaceae
description: The palms.

name: Asparagaceae
description: A varied family that includes mat-rushes (Lomandra), palm lilies and the weedy asparagus ferns.

name: Asphodelaceae
description: Includes flax-lilies, grass trees and bulbine lilies.

name: Asteraceae
description: The daisy family, the largest family of flowering plants. Its open flower heads offer easy nectar and pollen to many insects.

name: Balsaminaceae
description: Balsams and busy lizzies.

name: Berberidaceae
description: Barberries and nandina.

name: Bignoniaceae
description: Trumpet-flowered vines and trees, including bower and wonga vines and jacarandas.

name: Blechnaceae
description: Hard ferns and rasp ferns.

name: Boraginaceae
description: The borage family, whose blue flowers are favourites of honey bees.

name: Brassicaceae
description: The cabbage family: broccoli, cabbage, kale, rocket and mustards. Plants left to flower feed bees and hoverflies.

name: Bromeliaceae
description: Bromeliads: rosette plants whose leaf cups hold water.
care_note: Please flush the water out of the leaf cups every week in warm weather, so mosquitoes cannot breed in them.

name: Buxaceae
description: Box and its relatives.

name: Cannabaceae
description: Hemp, hops and hackberries, including the weedy Chinese elm (Celtis sinensis).

name: Caricaceae
description: Papaya (pawpaw) and its relatives.

name: Casuarinaceae
description: She-oaks: wind-pollinated trees whose cones feed black-cockatoos.

name: Commelinaceae
description: Spiderworts, including the weedy wandering trad (Tradescantia).

name: Convolvulaceae
description: The morning glory family, including sweet potato and the weedy blue morning glory.

name: Crassulaceae
description: Succulents such as jade plants, kalanchoes and the weedy mother-of-millions.

name: Cucurbitaceae
description: The gourd family: pumpkins, zucchini, cucumbers and melons. Most have separate male and female flowers and need bees to set fruit.

name: Cyperaceae
description: Sedges, which thrive in damp ground.

name: Dilleniaceae
description: Includes the guinea flowers (Hibbertia), whose flowers have no nectar and release pollen when buzzed by bees.

name: Doryanthaceae
description: The Gymea and spear lilies of eastern Australia.

name: Elaeocarpaceae
description: Includes blueberry ash and quandongs.

name: Ericaceae
description: The heath family, including blueberries, azaleas and many Australian heaths. Most need acidic soil.

name: Euphorbiaceae
description: The spurge family. Many members have milky sap.

toxic.note: The milky sap of many spurges irritates skin and eyes.

name: Fabaceae
description: The pea and wattle family. Most fix nitrogen in their roots, which enriches the soil.
fertiliser_note: Legumes make their own nitrogen, so they need little or no fertiliser.

name: Geraniaceae
description: Geraniums and pelargoniums.

name: Goodeniaceae
description: Fan-flowers and goodenias, with flowers shaped like a hand or a fan.

name: Haemodoraceae
description: Kangaroo paws and their relatives.

name: Hydrangeaceae
description: Hydrangeas and their relatives.

name: Iridaceae
description: The iris family, including wild irises (Dietes) and gladioli.

name: Juncaceae
description: Rushes, plants of wet ground and pond edges.

name: Lamiaceae
description: The mint family: aromatic herbs and shrubs such as lavender, salvias, rosemary, basil and coastal rosemary. Their flowers are favourites of bees.

name: Lauraceae
description: The laurel family, including avocados, bay trees and the weedy camphor laurel.

name: Malvaceae
description: The hibiscus family, which also includes flame trees and kurrajongs.

name: Melastomataceae
description: A mostly tropical family whose flowers are often buzz-pollinated.

name: Moraceae
description: The fig and mulberry family.

name: Musaceae
description: Bananas.

name: Myrtaceae
description: The myrtle family: eucalypts, bottlebrushes, paperbarks, tea trees and lilly pillies. Their flowers are rich in nectar and pollen.

name: Nyctaginaceae
description: Includes bougainvillea, whose colourful bracts surround small flowers.

name: Ochnaceae
description: Includes the weedy Mickey Mouse plant (Ochna).

name: Oleaceae
description: The olive family, including jasmines, privets and olives.

name: Oxalidaceae
description: Wood sorrels, several of which are garden weeds.

name: Passifloraceae
description: Passionfruit and other passion flowers.

name: Pittosporaceae
description: Pittosporums and the native frangipani.

name: Plantaginaceae
description: Plantains and their relatives.

name: Poaceae
description: The grasses. Most are wind-pollinated, so they offer bees little nectar, though some bees collect their pollen.

name: Portulacaceae
description: Portulaca and purslane.

name: Proteaceae
description: A mainly southern family of shrubs and trees, including grevilleas, banksias, hakeas and macadamias. Most are adapted to poor soils.
fertiliser_note: Phosphorus harms most Proteaceae. Please feed only with a native fertiliser labelled low in phosphorus, if at all.

compost.note: A thin layer of leaf mulch suits them better than rich compost.

name: Rosaceae
description: The rose family, which includes apples, pears, strawberries, stone fruit and berries.

name: Rubiaceae
description: The coffee family, including gardenias.

name: Rutaceae
description: The citrus family, which also includes correas, waxflowers and murraya. Many have aromatic leaves dotted with oil glands.

name: Sapindaceae
description: The soapberry family, including hop bushes, lychees and the weedy balloon vine.

name: Scrophulariaceae
description: Includes emu bushes (Eremophila) and boobiallas (Myoporum).

name: Solanaceae
description: The nightshade family: tomatoes, capsicums, eggplants and potatoes, as well as petunias and wild tobacco.

toxic.note: The leaves, stems and green fruit of many nightshades contain toxic alkaloids such as solanine.

name: Strelitziaceae
description: Bird of paradise plants.

name: Theaceae
description: The tea family, including camellias.

name: Tropaeolaceae
description: Nasturtiums.

name: Verbenaceae
description: The verbena family, which includes lantana and golden dewdrop.

name: Violaceae
description: Violets and pansies.

name: Zingiberaceae
description: The ginger family.
